item.title: U.S. and Israel Draw Up Plans for Renewed Strikes on Iran After Elections
item.description: Renewed hostilities might not be any more successful than the war’s first phase, and President Trump has repeatedly canceled plans for a return to major combat.
item.dc:creator: Julian E. Barnes, Eric Schmitt, Farnaz Fassihi, Natan Odenheimer and Ronen Bergman

United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Arash Khamooshi/Polaris for The New York Times

item.title: MAGA Bingo and Questions of Loyalty: 5 Michigan Senate Debate Takeaways
item.description: Abdul El-Sayed accused Mike Rogers of being overly devoted to President Trump. Mr. Rogers accused Dr. El-Sayed of not enough loyalty to the country. It was still more cordial than their last debate.
item.dc:creator: Reid J. Epstein
item.media:description: Dr. Abdul El-Sayed, left, and former Representative Mike Rogers are facing off in Michigan in one of this year’s most competitive Senate races.

item.title: Farmers, Health Care and Highways: 5 Takeaways from the Kansas Senate Debate
item.description: The Republican incumbent, Roger Marshall, is facing a surprisingly tough challenge from the Democratic nominee, Adam Hamilton.
item.dc:creator: Jess Bidgood and Lisa Lerer
item.media:description: Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas, right, a Republican, and his Democratic opponent, Adam Hamilton, participated in a debate Wednesday night.

item.title: Vance Defends Ramaswamy Ad Featuring Acton’s Mother Despite Backlash
item.description: The vice president backed an advertisement featuring Democrat Amy Acton’s mother, who has been estranged from Dr. Acton since her stepfather was charged with child rape.
item.dc:creator: Campbell Robertson and Bayliss Wagner
item.media:description: Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign for governor of Ohio was engulfed in controversy over an ad featuring the mother of his Democratic opponent.

item.title: Judge Restricts D.H.S. Field Operations Aimed at Unearthing Voter Fraud
item.description: The ruling largely blocked homeland security agents from carrying out field interviews in nine states, including California, as part of a sprawling effort to find noncitizens registered to vote.
item.dc:creator: Zach Montague and Shawn Hubler
item.media:credit: Philip Cheung for The New York Times
item.media:description: California voters casting ballots last November in a statewide special election.

item.title: In Trump’s Diplomacy, Insults Are a One-Way Street. Ukraine Is the Latest Example.
item.description: The latest rift with President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine serves as a reminder that President Trump readily lashes out at other world leaders, only to grow outraged if they fight back.
item.dc:creator: Peter Baker
item.media:description: President Trump’s belligerence leaves many world leaders reluctant to cross him for fear of blowback or even, depending on his mood, a fresh round of tariffs.

item.title: What Putin Gains From Releasing an American Prisoner
item.description: After Russia released an American prisoner, President Trump’s special envoy praised President Vladimir V. Putin as “a humanitarian.” Our White House and national security correspondent, David E. Sanger, describes how the release comes amid Mr. Trump’s broader shift toward Russia and away from Ukraine.
item.dc:creator: David E. Sanger, Nikolay Nikolov, Paul Abowd, Alexandra Ostasiewicz, Jon Miller, Rafaela Balster, Stephanie Swart and Whitney Shefte

item.title: When Starshield Cut Out, Ukrainian Drones Fell From the Skies
item.description: Ukraine says it still doesn’t know why the military satellite internet service, a sister to Starlink, was abruptly throttled, leaving troops vulnerable to Russian attacks.
item.dc:creator: Siobhán O’Grady, Carlotta Gall and Anton Troianovski
item.media:description: A Ukrainian soldier flying a drone in the Donetsk region last week. Members of the military have reported issues with drone connectivity since Starshield was disrupted.

item.title: How Mark Zuckerberg Pushed Meta to Shield Him From California’s Proposed Wealth Tax
item.description: The billionaire told Meta’s board that he planned to list his Silicon Valley home for sale. The company remade its stock structure to help him pay the tax if voters pass it.
item.dc:creator: Eli Tan and Theodore Schleifer
item.media:credit: Victor Llorente for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mark Zuckerberg, the chief executive of Meta, at his home in Lake Tahoe, Calif. He has another California home in Palo Alto, close to Meta’s headquarters.

item.title: Meta Ordered to Pay $25 Billion Over Cambridge Analytica Privacy Violations
item.description: The penalty, one of the largest levied against a tech giant, stemmed from a lawsuit by New Mexico claiming the social media company had misled users about their data privacy.
item.dc:creator: Eli Tan and Cecilia Kang
item.media:description: Meta’s annual Meta Connect event at the company’s Menlo Park, Calif., campus.

item.title: Meta Earnings Show Increased A.I. Spending, Even as Cash Pressures Grow
item.description: The spending has hurt the Silicon Valley giant’s cash flow, which turned negative. Meta said it would issue a new class of stock to help it raise more money.
item.dc:creator: Eli Tan
item.media:credit: Scott Ball for The New York Times
item.media:description: Construction of Meta’s Richland Parish Data Center in Holly Ridge, La.

item.title: Student Protests Mushroom Across Europe, Exposing Bleak Views of the Future
item.description: Since high school students began protesting in France in September, they’ve been joined by young demonstrators in at least seven other European countries.
item.dc:creator: Jason Horowitz
item.media:description: Protesters against the high cost of living in Athens, Greece, on Wednesday.

item.title: Looted Goods From French Stores Appear on Resale Sites After Riots
item.description: Officials in France are pressing online platforms like eBay and Vinted to remove items that were stolen during public disturbances over the weekend.
item.dc:creator: Jenny Gross
item.media:description: People smashing a store on a day of demonstrations against the cost of living and rising fuel prices in Paris.

item.title: Cornell Case Highlights Shifting Federal Title IX Enforcement
item.description: From Barack Obama to Donald Trump, ideology has infused the interpretation of the federal law banning sex discrimination on college campuses.
item.dc:creator: Michael C. Bender
item.media:credit: Lauren Petracca for The New York Times
item.media:description: An allegation of a gang rape at Cornell in 2024 has put renewed attention on the 54-year-old law known as Title IX.

item.title: Oregon Teacher Disputes Account of Her Heroism During School Shooting
item.description: Becky Drury, who was said to have shielded a student during a deadly shooting in Bend, refuted the account. “The truth is I was shot before I had any chance to act.”
item.dc:creator: Anna Griffin
item.category: Silver Rail Elementary, Bend, Ore, Shooting (2026)
item.media:credit: Jordan Gale for The New York Times
item.media:description: Last week, a teenage gunman fatally shot three children and one teacher at Silver Rail Elementary School in Bend, Ore.

item.title: Why a Pillar of Christian Journalism is in Turmoil
item.description: Former employees of Christianity Today say new leadership has been pushing back on independent journalism. About half of its staff members have left or been laid off over 14 months.
item.dc:creator: Ruth Graham
item.media:credit: Justin Merriman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Bonnie Kristian, Christianity Today’s deputy editor until recently, said the outlet displays “an increasingly muddled sense of its place within American evangelicalism.”

item.title: Trump Asks Supreme Court to Allow Border Wall Construction in Big Bend
item.description: A lower court judge had halted the administration’s plan to erect hundreds of miles of barriers in the Big Bend region of Texas.
item.dc:creator: Abbie VanSickle
item.media:description: People protest the plans by President Donald Trump’s administration to build a section of the border wall at the Big Bend National Park, in Study Butte, Texas, in August.

item.title: Supreme Court Blocks Trump From Denying Gender-Affirming Care to Trans Prisoners
item.description: The justices, for now, agreed to continue preventing the Bureau of Prisons from implementing a policy that would prohibit gender-transition medical treatments.
item.dc:creator: Ann E. Marimow
item.media:description: Guards on the steps of the Supreme Court on Monday.

item.title: ‘Open War’ Between Afghanistan and Pakistan Adds a Volatile Element
item.description: The two sides turn to proxy groups after eight months of a conflict that has taken a heavy toll on civilians.
item.dc:creator: Elian Peltier
item.media:credit: Tomas Munita for The New York Times
item.media:description: A house hit in June by Pakistani airstrikes in Paktia Province, Afghanistan, near the border with Pakistan, as seen in August.

item.title: For an Experiment in Political Affirmative Action, Look to Taiwan
item.description: The island adopted quotas for women running for public office decades before other countries. The upshot? Today, few of them need quotas to get elected.
item.dc:creator: Li Yuan
item.media:credit: Lam Yik Fei for The New York Times
item.media:description: Su Chiao-hui campaigning for a mayoral post in Taiwan. Women hold 42 percent of Taiwan’s legislative seats, the highest share in Asia and comparable to Nordic countries.

item.title: Palestinian Voters Could Determine Israel’s Future
item.description: Palestinian citizens may have the electoral weight to influence Israeli politics, even as they feel they have so little control over their lives.

item.title: Delhi’s Winter Season of Polluted Air Begins
item.description: As air quality plummeted in India’s largest city, the government said it would act to curtail the haze that blankets the capital every winter.
item.dc:creator: Anupreeta Das
item.media:description: Hazy skies in New Delhi on Wednesday.
